newsitem.title: USA: Star Louisiana refinery unit down, NYMEX up.
newsitem.headline: Star Louisiana refinery unit down, NYMEX up.

text.p: Firefighters early Thursday extinguished the blaze at Star Enterprise's Convent, Louisiana refinery which shut down a 40,000 barrel-a-day H-oil unit, a company spokesman said.

The H-oil unit process heavy feedstocks, such as residual fuel, into lighter products including No. 2 heating oil and even gasoline, and NYMEX heating oil futures prices surged in early Thursday action on the news of the fire.
Cash market traders said cash values firmed slightly but acknowledged that the effects of the outage were not yet clear.

"I'm getting some contradictory statements," said one heating oil and jet fuel trader, who noted heating oil and diesel differentials in Houston spot markets firmed slightly but not dramatically amid the uncertainty.

No other units at the refinery were damaged by the fire, and refinery output, normally 225,000 bpd, was "marginally less than that," said Star spokesman Shawn Frederick. The company previously estimated crude runs were reduced by 20 percent.

The fire on the recovery side of the H-oil unit started at 1800 CST/0000 GMT was put out shortly before 0200 CST/800 GMT Thursday, according to Frederick. No estimates on the how long the unit would be out of service were available.

Three women were treated for possible exposure to sulphur dioxide and released, Frederick said. No clear information was available on the possible pollutant emissions from the fire at the refinery, which is located in a sugar cane field on the Mississippi River between New Orleans and Baton Rouge.
Star is a joint venture of Texaco Inc and Saudi Refinery Inc.
